## Scope and principal findings

This covers **the Lindt & Sprüngli corporate group**, including Lindt, Ghirardelli, Russell Stover, Whitman’s, Pangburn’s, Caffarel, Hofbauer and Küfferle. It does **not** include the separate business Confiserie Sprüngli. I used the **2025 Integrated Annual Report**, published in March 2026, and the group’s and brands’ own websites first. ([lindt-spruengli.com](https://www.lindt-spruengli.com/amfile/file/download/id/10512/file/Integrated-Annual-Report-2025.pdf))

**The group does more than manufacture and retail chocolate.** Its documented activities include non-chocolate confectionery; dessert and beverage ingredients, including caramel and vanilla products; café and ice-cream operations; branded liqueur; foodservice accessories; licensing; property-related income; and administrative and demonstration-production services. The evidence for each is below.

**Completeness qualification:** this is a comprehensive inventory of the activities identifiable in the public sources reviewed—not a claim that the company publishes every incidental activity or every product’s destination countries. In particular, **a complete product-by-country sales matrix is not publicly stated**. I distinguish confirmed markets from countries that are not disclosed, and do not assume that every product is sold throughout Lindt’s global network.

## 1. Products and customer-facing activities

In the table, “direct buyer” means the purchaser from a group company—not necessarily the person buying from a downstream supermarket or distributor. Where the sources establish a distribution channel but not contractual customer relationships, I say so.

| Activity / product or service | Who buys directly from the group? | Ultimate consumer and how it reaches them | Countries of sale, particularly the EEA |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1. Finished chocolate and chocolate confectionery.** Bars, truffles, pralines, filled chocolates, boxed assortments, seasonal figures and gifts, and chocolate/hazelnut spreads and snacks. Brands include Lindt and the acquired brands listed above. | Retailers, wholesalers and independent distributors; also consumers buying through group shops and e-shops. | Consumers and gift recipients. Sold through supermarkets, other grocery retailers, club/discounter formats, third-party online retailers, group shops/e-shops and airport/travel-retail channels. Wholesale is the largest channel. | Lindt states availability in **more than 120 countries**, but does not name all of them. Confirmed country markets are listed in §2. **Do not apply this 120-country statement to every brand or SKU.** Hofbauer/Küfferle have an Austrian focus; Caffarel states distribution in more than 40 foreign countries without identifying them all. ([lindt-spruengli.com](https://www.lindt-spruengli.com/company/at-a-glance/)) |
| **2. Non-chocolate sugar confectionery—Caffarel.** Hard candies, fruit jellies, including organic variants and jellies with 65% fruit. | Caffarel identifies qualified distributors and directs consumers to shops. Its product pages do not specify which retailers buy directly versus through distributors. | Consumers, through confectionery shops and other retail outlets. | **Italy is evidenced by its Italian retail offering.** Caffarel’s overall international distribution covers more than 40 foreign countries, but **the countries of sale of these candy ranges are not stated**; no complete EEA list is provided. ([caffarel.com](https://caffarel.com/nostri-prodotti/caramelle/bonta-pura/)) |
| **3. Non-chocolate sugar confectionery—Russell Stover.** Examples include pectin jelly beans and sugar-free lemon hard candy. | Consumers directly through its online shop; corporate-gift customers are also offered jelly beans. The cited pages do not establish the direct wholesale buyers for these particular products. | Consumers and gift recipients; online and through the brand’s retail network. | **United States is the evidenced market. Countries outside the US, including EEA countries, are not stated for these products.** ([russellstover.com](https://www.russellstover.com/)) |
| **4. Candied chestnuts—Caffarel Marrons Glacés.** A separate confectionery category, not merely chocolate-covered candy. | Caffarel’s distributor/retail network; precise direct-purchaser relationships for this range are not disclosed. | Consumers and gift recipients, through confectionery/gift retail. | Offered on Caffarel’s **Italian** website and store-finder system. **Other countries of sale, including a full EEA list, are not stated for this range.** ([caffarel.com](https://caffarel.com/)) |
| **5. Baking and professional chocolate/cocoa ingredients—Ghirardelli.** Chocolate chips and wafers, cocoa powders, sweet-ground powders, hot-cocoa products and chocolate sauces. | Foodservice distributors and supply retailers; foodservice operators can also place direct orders with Ghirardelli. These include specialty-coffee businesses, restaurants and chefs. | Diners and beverage customers consume the ingredients in prepared desserts, drinks and other foods. Home consumers also buy baking/topping products. Sold directly by the professional sales team, through distributors, restaurant-supply stores and online. | **US is the clearly evidenced market. A complete international country list is not stated; EEA sales are not established by these sources.** The sources do not establish a separate general-purpose bulk supply business to industrial chocolate manufacturers. ([ghirardelli.com](https://www.ghirardelli.com/professional-sauces-information)) |
| **6. Non-chocolate dessert/beverage sauces—Ghirardelli.** Caramel, sea-salt caramel and vanilla sauces. Caramel is also sold in a consumer squeeze bottle. | Foodservice distributors, supply retailers and operators ordering directly; consumers directly through Ghirardelli’s e-shop for retail-format products. | Café/restaurant customers and home consumers. Used in coffee drinks, desserts, ice cream and baking; sold through professional distribution and retail/online channels. | **US confirmed.** Ghirardelli’s own e-shop does not support international shipping. **Professional export countries and EEA destinations are not stated.** The caramel product’s ingredient list confirms that this is genuinely a non-cocoa product. ([ghirardelli.com](https://www.ghirardelli.com/professional-sauces-information)) |
| **7. Beverage mixes, including non-chocolate mixes—Ghirardelli.** Frappé mixes include Classic White and Vanilla, alongside chocolate, frozen-hot-cocoa, mocha and white-mocha variants. | Professional distributors/supply retailers and foodservice operators purchasing directly. | Customers of cafés, restaurants and other beverage operators, in prepared blended drinks. | **US evidenced. Other countries of sale, particularly in the EEA, are not stated in the professional catalogue or ordering pages.** ([ghirardelli.com](https://www.ghirardelli.com/media/wysiwyg/Ghirardelli_PPD_Full_Line_Brochure.pdf)) |
| **8. Compound confectionery coatings—Ghirardelli.** Premium Coating Wafers in Dark, Milk and White varieties; no tempering required. This is distinct from selling conventional chocolate couverture. | Distributors and professional users; Ghirardelli explicitly offers direct sales. | Consumers of coated strawberries, cookies, desserts and decorated confectionery. Sold in professional bags and bulk cases through distributors, online and directly. | **US-oriented offering. Complete countries of sale and EEA destinations are not stated.** ([ghirardelli.com](https://www.ghirardelli.com/professional/premium-coating-wafers?naviga_item_id=21668)) |
| **9. Café, beverage and dessert service.** Lindt outlets sell prepared hot/cold chocolate, coffee, milkshakes and ice cream; café menus also document tea, juice, soft drinks, cakes, brownies, macarons and other desserts. Ghirardelli operates Ice Cream & Chocolate Shops. | Consumers directly at the outlets. | The purchasers themselves or their companions. Counter service, takeaway and, depending on location, seated café service. | **Australia** is confirmed by Lindt’s current boutique page and linked drinks offering; **US** by Ghirardelli’s shop network. **Italy—an EEA country—is additionally confirmed by reporting on Lindt’s Milan shop selling coffee, frappés and ice cream. Switzerland** is covered separately below. **A complete country list for café/ice-cream services is not stated.** Older official menus establish the broader assortment, not guaranteed current availability at every outlet. ([lindt.com.au](https://www.lindt.com.au/lindt-chocolate-boutique-warringah-mall)) |
| **10. Café catering/private-event food service at Lindt Home of Chocolate.** An official event brochure includes salads, soups and savoury dishes, not just chocolate desserts. It identifies Lindt & Sprüngli (Schweiz) AG. | Private-event organisers and guests; the brochure does not fully explain the contractual booking/payment arrangements. | Event attendees. Prepared catering/café food service. | **Kilchberg, Switzerland. No EEA location or wider country network is stated for this service.** This should not be confused with ownership of the museum itself. ([lindt-home-of-chocolate.com](https://www.lindt-home-of-chocolate.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/Eventbrochure_A4_English.pdf)) |
| **11. Alcoholic beverages—Caffarel branded liqueur.** Gianduia 1865 liqueur; retail evidence also documents a chocolate-and-rum liqueur. | The direct contractual buyers are not identified. Retail distribution is evidenced; whether the liqueur is manufactured internally or by a supplier is not disclosed in the sources reviewed. | Adult consumers and gift recipients. Bottled, gift-boxed products sold through confectionery retailers and wine/liquor shops. | **Italy confirmed**, including Italian delivery by a retailer. **Other countries of sale and a complete EEA list are not stated.** The company’s own website confirms the branded product; retailers add format/channel information. ([caffarel.com](https://caffarel.com/)) |
| **12. Non-food foodservice accessories—Ghirardelli.** Sauce-bottle pumps and two-/three-tier sauce racks appear as orderable items in its professional catalogue. | Professional distributors and foodservice customers; the catalogue does not identify the direct buyer for each accessory. | Used by baristas, kitchen staff and foodservice operators—not eaten by consumers. Sold alongside professional sauces through the professional ordering/distribution system. | **US-oriented catalogue. Other countries of sale, including EEA countries, are not stated.** ([ghirardelli.com](https://www.ghirardelli.com/media/wysiwyg/Ghirardelli_PPD_Full_Line_Brochure.pdf)) |
| **13. Corporate gifting, personalisation and fulfilment.** Gift assortments, personalised boxes, business-card/greeting-card insertion and multi-address shipping. This is a service/channel overlay on the food business, rather than a separate food category. | Businesses buying employee/client gifts, event organisers and individual consumers. | Employees, clients, event guests and other gift recipients. Direct online ordering and specialist corporate-gifting teams. | **US confirmed** for Ghirardelli and Russell Stover; Ghirardelli explicitly limits multi-address shipping to the contiguous US. **The reviewed sources do not state a complete international or EEA country list for group-wide corporate-gifting services.** ([ghirardelli.com](https://www.ghirardelli.com/businessgifting)) |

## 2. Confirmed chocolate sales markets—especially the EEA

The group’s own **“Shop with us”** directory confirms Lindt country-market offerings in these EEA countries:

**Austria, Bulgaria, Czechia, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, Hungary, Italy, Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Slovakia, Spain and Sweden.** This establishes market availability, not that every linked site provides online checkout or sells the same range. ([lindt-spruengli.com](https://www.lindt-spruengli.com/shop-with-us/))

Additional official evidence identifies **Belgium and Portugal** through the Benelux and Iberian market operations and reported sales growth; **Ireland** has a Dublin representative office within the UK operation. The directory of offices is evidence of commercial organisation, but is not a product-by-country catalogue. ([lindt-spruengli.com](https://www.lindt-spruengli.com/amfile/file/download/id/10287/file/Lindt-Spruengli-Media-Release-Sales-2025-EN.pdf))

**Not established individually by the sources reviewed:** Croatia, Cyprus, Estonia, Greece, Iceland, Latvia, Liechtenstein, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Romania and Slovenia. This means **their individual country sales are not stated here—not that Lindt does not sell there**. The statement that Lindt is available in over 120 countries is insufficient to identify the missing markets or their product ranges. ([lindt-spruengli.com](https://www.lindt-spruengli.com/company/at-a-glance/))

Outside the EEA, the official shopping directory confirms **Australia, Brazil, Canada, China, Japan, Mexico, South Africa, Switzerland, the United Kingdom and the United States**. The annual report also describes retail expansion into **Chile and New Zealand**. **The full global list is not stated.** ([lindt-spruengli.com](https://www.lindt-spruengli.com/shop-with-us/))

## 3. Other revenue-generating activities disclosed in the annual report

These ancillary activities matter because they would be missed by treating the group solely as a chocolate manufacturer.

| Activity | Product/service, direct customer and ultimate beneficiary | Sales mechanism and geography |
|---|---|---|
| **Licensing/royalties** | The report records royalty income but does not identify every licence or licensee. A documented example is **Ghirardelli-branded baking mixes associated with The Krusteaz Company**; the business customer is the licensee, while home bakers and foodservice diners ultimately consume the resulting products. | Contractual licensing, followed by the licensee’s retail/foodservice distribution. **US evidenced; full licensing territories and EEA countries are not stated.** These mixes should not automatically be described as manufactured and sold directly by Lindt & Sprüngli. ([lindt-spruengli.com](https://www.lindt-spruengli.com/amfile/file/download/id/10512/file/Integrated-Annual-Report-2025.pdf)) |
| **Property/building-right and rental activities** | The group receives ground rent for the building right granted to the **Lindt Chocolate Competence Foundation**, and has rental arrangements with it. The direct customer is the foundation; its operations benefit from use of the property. | Bilateral property contracts in **Switzerland**. Other rental/subleasing customer countries are **not stated** in the cited disclosure. ([lindt-spruengli.com](https://www.lindt-spruengli.com/amfile/file/download/id/10512/file/Integrated-Annual-Report-2025.pdf)) |
| **Administrative services** | Services supplied to the chocolate and cocoa foundations and named pension-related foundations/funds. These entities are the direct recipients and beneficiaries. | Related-party service arrangements. The report identifies the counterparties, but **does not state a country-of-sale breakdown; no EEA external-service market is disclosed**. ([lindt-spruengli.com](https://www.lindt-spruengli.com/amfile/file/download/id/10512/file/Integrated-Annual-Report-2025.pdf)) |
| **Show-production services** | Chocolate-making demonstrations for Lindt Home of Chocolate, paid for by the **Lindt Chocolate Competence Foundation**; museum visitors are the ultimate audience. | Contracted demonstration production in **Kilchberg, Switzerland**. **No other countries are stated.** ([lindt-spruengli.com](https://www.lindt-spruengli.com/amfile/file/download/id/10512/file/Integrated-Annual-Report-2025.pdf)) |
| **Other third-party fees** | The report confirms this income category but does not describe all underlying services, customers or beneficiaries. | **Products/services, channels and countries of sale are not sufficiently stated to classify further.** ([lindt-spruengli.com](https://www.lindt-spruengli.com/amfile/file/download/id/10512/file/Integrated-Annual-Report-2025.pdf)) |

## 4. Important boundaries

- **Cocoa processing is also an internal production activity.** The group sources cocoa inputs and produces cocoa mass for its chocolate operations, except Russell Stover, which purchases finished mass/products. This does **not by itself establish external sales of cocoa mass, cocoa butter or commodity cocoa powder to industrial manufacturers**. External Ghirardelli professional cocoa products are covered above. ([lindt-spruengli.com](https://www.lindt-spruengli.com/company/from-bean-to-bar/))
- **Confiserie Sprüngli is independent.** Its pastry, restaurant and other activities must not be attributed to this group. ([lindt-spruengli.com](https://www.lindt-spruengli.com/sustainability/faqs/))
- **Lindt Home of Chocolate is a foundation project**, not simply a group-owned museum business. Museum admissions, educational activities and the pilot plant should not automatically be counted as group sales; the group’s documented catering, property and compensated demonstration activities are distinguished above. ([lindt-spruengli.com](https://www.lindt-spruengli.com/sustainability/faqs/))

**Bottom line:** the group’s non-chocolate activities are real, but their geographical disclosure is much less complete than that of the core Lindt chocolate business. For most ancillary ranges, especially within the EEA, the defensible answer is **“countries of sale are not stated”**, rather than assuming distribution throughout the group’s 120-plus-country chocolate network.

# Ritter Sport: business-activity inventory

**Scope:** I treat “Ritter Sport” primarily as **Alfred Ritter GmbH & Co. KG and its food-business operations**, not automatically as every enterprise owned by members of the Ritter family. I separately cover the related energy businesses because they are important activities outside chocolate, but should not be confused with the chocolate manufacturer. The company’s website identifies Alfred Ritter GmbH & Co. KG as its operator. ([ritter-sport.com](https://www.ritter-sport.com/imprint))

**Source limitation:** I started with the company’s website and its **Sustainability Reports 2023/2024 and 2021/2022**. I did not obtain a freely accessible, complete consolidated financial annual report: a registry-information service lists consolidated accounts for 2024, but access to the document is paid. Accordingly, this is an inventory of **all activities identified in the public sources reviewed**, not a guarantee that every subsidiary’s incidental revenue stream has been captured. ([irp.cdn-website.com](https://irp.cdn-website.com/6cb74a62/files/uploaded/NHB_2024_EN_Web.pdf))

Countries below are distinguished as **confirmed sales locations**, **markets indicated by packaging**, or **not stated**. Production locations are not treated as proof of sales there.

## 1. Food products and direct-to-consumer businesses

### A. Ritter Sport packaged chocolate and chocolate confectionery

- **Product:** Chocolate bars, including milk, white, dark, filled, nut, vegan and protein varieties; large bars, miniatures, seasonal/limited editions and gift assortments. Other formats include chocolate cubes and Rum crispy pieces. These are product families within the same confectionery business, rather than separate industries. ([ritter-sport.com](https://www.ritter-sport.com/Product))
- **Direct buyers:** Retail trade customers are documented. Wholesalers/importers/distributors are also part of the distribution chain, although the reviewed sources do not provide a complete allocation of which customers buy directly from Alfred Ritter versus its local sales companies. Consumers buy directly in company shops and through its webshop. ([irp.cdn-website.com](https://irp.cdn-website.com/6cb74a62/files/uploaded/NHB_2024_EN_Web.pdf))
- **Ultimate consumers:** Individual consumers and recipients of gifts.
- **How sold:** Food retail/supermarkets; wholesale distribution; company shops in Waldenbuch and Berlin; the company webshop; and airport duty-free/travel retail. Norway’s airport retailer, for example, lists travel-retail-exclusive towers, miniatures and chocolate cubes. ([blog.ritter-sport.de](https://blog.ritter-sport.de/2016/03/07/das-neue-ritter-sport-sortiment/comment-page-7/))
- **Countries:** The company says **more than 100 countries**, but **does not publish a complete country-of-sale list in the sources reviewed**. Germany, Italy, the United Kingdom and the United States are evidenced by its shops, Italian sales operation/catalogue and corporate report; Ireland is identified by its UK & Ireland management; Norway is confirmed by the airport retailer. These are examples, not the whole geographical footprint. **I could not establish a complete EEA country list or product-by-country matrix.** ([ritter-sport.com](https://www.ritter-sport.com/about-us))

### B. Amicelli wafer confectionery

- **Product:** Cream-filled, chocolate-covered wafer rolls under the **Amicelli** brand, including hazelnut, milk and coconut variants. This is distinct from the Ritter Sport bar containing an Amicelli-inspired filling. ([amicelli.com](https://www.amicelli.com/))
- **Direct buyers:** Trade customers; the company’s commercial catalogue provides a product-request facility. The precise retailer/wholesaler/direct-consumer sales split is **not stated**. ([innovation.ritter-sport.com](https://innovation.ritter-sport.com/standardproducts/amicelli_hazelnut_))
- **Ultimate consumers:** Consumers eating the wafers, including gift recipients.
- **How sold:** Packaged consumer confectionery supplied through the trade; commercial orders/enquiries through Ritter’s catalogue. ([innovation.ritter-sport.com](https://innovation.ritter-sport.com/standardproducts/amicelli_hazelnut_))
- **Countries:** Its catalogue’s **“country foil” entries indicate packaging intended for**:
  - **EEA:** Germany, Austria, Netherlands, France, Belgium, Spain, Portugal, Poland, Czechia, Slovakia, Romania and Croatia.
  - **Outside the EEA:** Switzerland, United Kingdom, Russia, Belarus and Kazakhstan.
  
  These packaging entries are **not confirmation of current sales in every listed country**. English, Hebrew and Arabic language versions also appear, but language alone does not establish destination countries. **A complete actual country-of-sale list is not stated.** ([innovation.ritter-sport.com](https://innovation.ritter-sport.com/standardproducts/amicelli_hazelnut_))

### C. Bespoke chocolate, shop-exclusive products and small-batch manufacture

- **Product/service:** Custom chocolate bars made with customers’ selected ingredients and personalised packaging; handmade chocolate from the Berlin shop’s small manufactory; exclusive and limited products. The older report also describes shop-only “upcycling” editions incorporating visually imperfect but otherwise usable chocolate. ([ritter-sport.com](https://www.ritter-sport.com/de/berlin))
- **Direct buyers:** Consumers visiting the shops.
- **Ultimate consumers:** Buyers themselves or gift recipients.
- **How sold:** Directly in company shops; Berlin’s chocolate makers produce selected combinations in front of the customer. ([ritter-sport.com](https://www.ritter-sport.com/de/berlin))
- **Countries:** **Germany**, specifically Berlin and Waldenbuch for the documented shop-exclusive business. **Other countries of sale are not stated.** ([ritter-sport.com](https://www.ritter-sport.com/waldenbuch))

### D. Corporate gifts and promotional chocolate

- **Product/service:** Standard chocolate in bulk and customised products with individually designed wrappers, envelope packaging and seasonal gift formats; advice and tailored shipping arrangements. ([b2b.ritter-sport.com](https://b2b.ritter-sport.com/))
- **Direct buyers:** Businesses and organisations purchasing promotional products, corporate gifts or bulk chocolate—not necessarily food retailers.
- **Ultimate consumers:** The businesses’ customers, employees, event attendees and other recipients.
- **How sold:** Direct B2B quotations and orders through the dedicated business-customer website, contact form and telephone. ([b2b.ritter-sport.com](https://b2b.ritter-sport.com/))
- **Countries:** **Countries of sale/delivery are not stated** on the reviewed B2B page. A German-language website and German contract law should not be taken as proof that delivery is restricted to Germany. ([b2b.ritter-sport.com](https://b2b.ritter-sport.com/))

### E. CacaoVida non-chocolate beverages

- **Product:** Cocoa-fruit lemonade, cocoa-fruit iced tea and **CacaoVida Secco**, an alcoholic sparkling drink made from cocoa-fruit juice rather than grapes. The company’s current CacaoVida profile emphasises fruit-juice lemonades; the wider three-product range is documented in the 2021/2022 report. **Continued availability of every older SKU was not verified.** ([de.linkedin.com](https://de.linkedin.com/company/cacaovida))
- **Direct buyers:** Consumers directly; hospitality outlets are documented as sales locations, although whether every outlet purchases directly rather than through an intermediary is **not stated**. ([blog.ritter-sport.de](https://blog.ritter-sport.de/2021/07/29/cacaovida/))
- **Ultimate consumers:** Beverage consumers; adults for Secco.
- **How sold:** Ritter Sport shops in Waldenbuch and Berlin, online, and selected hospitality venues around Stuttgart. A CacaoVida-branded ale was also developed **in collaboration with SinghBräu**; this should be described as a beverage collaboration, not proof that Ritter operates a brewery. ([blog.ritter-sport.de](https://blog.ritter-sport.de/2021/07/29/cacaovida/))
- **Countries:** **Germany** is documented. **Sales in other EEA countries and a complete delivery-country list are not stated.** Nicaragua is the juice’s source, not evidence of a consumer sales market. ([blog.ritter-sport.de](https://blog.ritter-sport.de/2021/07/29/cacaovida/))

### F. Chocolate-making workshops and visitor experiences

- **Service:** Chocolate-making workshops for families, friends, colleagues and groups, alongside educational chocolate/cocoa exhibitions. These are visitor/educational services, not simply chocolate sales. ([ritter-sport.com](https://www.ritter-sport.com/waldenbuch))
- **Direct buyers:** Individuals, families and group organisers; corporate customers can book group experiences.
- **Ultimate users:** Workshop participants and exhibition visitors.
- **How sold:** Direct bookings, including online workshop booking. **The reviewed material does not establish a separate admission charge for every exhibition**, so exhibition access should not automatically be treated as a paid revenue stream. ([ritter-sport.com](https://www.ritter-sport.com/waldenbuch))
- **Countries:** Services are delivered in **Germany**, at Waldenbuch and Berlin. Customers’ countries of residence are **not stated**. ([ritter-sport.com](https://www.ritter-sport.com/waldenbuch))

### G. Bistro/foodservice and event-space hire

- **Product/service:** Berlin’s Bunte Schokowelt sells prepared food and beverages, including homemade Ritter Sport cake, ice cream and hot chocolate, for on-site consumption or takeaway. It also offers a bookable event area for private and business events. ([ritter-sport.com](https://www.ritter-sport.com/de/berlin))
- **Direct buyers:** Bistro customers; private event organisers and corporate event customers.
- **Ultimate consumers/users:** Diners, takeaway customers and event attendees.
- **How sold:** Directly through the Berlin bistro and by arrangement for event bookings.
- **Countries:** **Germany—Berlin. Other operating/sales countries are not stated.** ([ritter-sport.com](https://www.ritter-sport.com/de/berlin))

### H. Non-food gifts and merchandise

- **Product:** Company shops sell gift items in addition to chocolate. Company promotional material identifies branded bags, keyrings and lanyards, demonstrating a non-food merchandise range, although it does not establish that every promotional item is always sold separately. ([ritter-sport.com](https://www.ritter-sport.com/waldenbuch))
- **Direct buyers:** Shop visitors.
- **Ultimate users:** Buyers and gift recipients.
- **How sold:** Directly through the company’s visitor shops.
- **Countries:** **Germany—Waldenbuch and Berlin. Merchandise-specific online availability and other delivery countries are not stated.** ([ritter-sport.com](https://www.ritter-sport.com/waldenbuch))

## 2. Upstream and internal operations—not necessarily external sales businesses

| Activity | Product/service; direct buyer and ultimate use | Route and countries |
|---|---|---|
| **Cocoa cultivation and post-harvest operations** | El Cacao grows cocoa in Nicaragua and supplies the group’s chocolate-making chain; cocoa-fruit juice also enters CacaoVida products. Ultimate consumers eat the chocolate or drink the beverages. **External buyers of plantation output are not identified.** | Integrated supply chain rather than a documented public wholesale offer. Cultivation is in **Nicaragua**; **external countries of sale for beans/juice are not stated**. ([ritter-sport.com](https://www.ritter-sport.com/our-cocoa)) |
| **Hazelnut cultivation** | Ritter Agrar grows hazelnuts in south-west France to contribute to Ritter’s own ingredient requirements. **No external buyer list is stated.** Ultimate users are consumers of nut-containing products. | Internal ingredient supply. **France** is confirmed in the company report. A secondary source also reports a hazelnut subsidiary in **Chile**, but I did not verify its detailed operations from a primary source. **External sale countries are not stated.** ([irp.cdn-website.com](https://irp.cdn-website.com/6cb74a62/files/uploaded/NHB_2022_EN_online.pdf)) |
| **Electricity and heat generation** | Own wind, photovoltaic, solar-thermal and combined-heat-and-power facilities supply operational energy. The identified user is the company itself; **external energy customers are not disclosed**. | Primarily captive energy supply. **Countries of external electricity/heat sale are not stated**; the sources do not establish a separate retail utility business. ([ritter-sport.com](https://www.ritter-sport.com/de/energie-emissionen)) |
| **Packaging, warehousing and internal logistics** | Packaging chocolate into retail-ready boxes/displays, storing materials/products and transporting them between sites. The report describes the Reichenbach packaging operation being brought in-house in April 2024. **No third-party service customers are identified.** | Internal operations in **Germany**, supporting the confectionery business. **Countries of sale for standalone logistics/packaging services are not stated**, and such external sales were not established. ([irp.cdn-website.com](https://irp.cdn-website.com/6cb74a62/files/uploaded/NHB_2024_EN_Web.pdf)) |

**Important negative finding:** I found no substantiated public offer by Ritter Sport of bulk cocoa butter, cocoa powder, cocoa liquor or couverture sold independently to food manufacturers or artisans. Its sourcing website describes ingredient procurement and processing partners, not an external ingredient-sales catalogue. This is **“not established,” not proof that no incidental B2B sales occur**. ([ritter-sport.com](https://www.ritter-sport.com/cocoa-sourcing))

## 3. Historical or limited-project activities outside mainstream chocolate

### PURmacherei: oat/almond snacks and cocoa-bean snacks — discontinued

- **Product:** Hand-made **HaferHAPS** oat-and-almond snack balls, including non-chocolate varieties; also chocolate-coated and caramelised cocoa-bean snacks marketed under names including KakaoCHOCS/KakaoWUMMS.
- **Direct buyers / ultimate consumers:** Retail trade customers and consumers buying directly; individual snack consumers.
- **How sold:** Own online shop and stationary retail.
- **Countries:** Germany is evidenced by the business’s market context and retail activity; **a complete country-of-sale list is not stated**.
- **Status:** Its own company profile says business activity **ceased completely on August 31, 2024**. It should therefore not be presented as a current Ritter Sport business. ([foodinnovationcamp.de](https://foodinnovationcamp.de/purmacherei-reduziert-snacks-auf-das-wesentliche/))

### Digital collectibles/NFTs — documented 2023 project

- **Product/service:** The **ART OF THE SQUARE** collection of 256 digital collectibles, with associated benefits depending on category.
- **Direct buyers / ultimate users:** Individual purchasers with Ethereum wallets; collectible holders and eligible benefit recipients.
- **How sold:** Direct primary sale through Ritter’s NFT platform. Subsequent holder-to-holder marketplace trading is distinct from a direct Ritter sale.
- **Countries:** **A complete NFT-purchaser country list is not stated.** The company’s terms explicitly restricted associated benefits to residents of **Germany and Austria**. The terms refer to the September 14, 2023 reveal; this is a documented limited project, not verified ongoing NFT issuance. ([ritter-sport.com](https://www.ritter-sport.com/de/rechtliche_hinweise))

The company also historically produced **jelly confectionery, fondant and refreshment sticks** during cocoa shortages beginning in 1935. These are historical activities, not current product lines; **direct-buyer categories and countries of sale are not stated** in the company history. ([ritter-sport.com](https://www.ritter-sport.com/history))

## 4. Related Ritter-family energy businesses—separate from the food company

Ritter Solartechnik names Alfred T. Ritter and Marli Hoppe-Ritter as principal shareholders. That establishes the family relationship, but **does not by itself establish that Alfred Ritter GmbH & Co. KG owns these companies**. They are therefore listed separately rather than silently consolidated into Ritter Sport’s food-business inventory. ([ritter-solartechnik.de](https://www.ritter-solartechnik.de/hauptgesellschafter/))

| Activity | Product/service | Direct buyers → ultimate users | Sales route and countries |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Heating-system manufacture and specialist distribution** | Solar thermal systems, heat pumps, pellet and gas heating, heat stores and controls. | Installer/specialist trade customers → households and building users. | Manufacturer/specialist-trade supply and professional webshop. **Germany is documented; a complete current country-of-sale list is not stated.** ([ritter-energie.de](https://ritter-energie.de/)) |
| **PV, storage and electrical-system distribution** | Photovoltaics, battery storage, connection/backup equipment and energy-management products; a PV-rental offering for installers. | Professional installers → property owners and electricity users. | B2B specialist distribution/webshop. **Complete sale countries, especially the EEA breakdown, are not stated in the reviewed pages.** ([ritter-energie.de](https://ritter-energie.de/)) |
| **OEM solar-thermal components** | Vacuum-tube collectors and associated mounting technology supplied to heating-industry manufacturers. | Heating-equipment manufacturers → users of their finished systems. | Direct industrial/OEM supply. **Countries of sale are not stated** in the reviewed company description. ([ritter-solartechnik.de](https://www.ritter-solartechnik.de/ueber-uns/)) |
| **Large-scale solar-thermal systems—Ritter XL Solar** | Solar heat for industrial/agricultural processes and district-heating networks. | Commercial, industrial and heat-network project customers → factories and connected heat users. | Project-based system supply. Actual projects are documented in **Germany, Austria and Switzerland**. A company-supplied directory lists additional markets, but those are **market declarations, not proof of completed sales in each country**. ([ritter-solartechnik.de](https://www.ritter-solartechnik.de/ueber-uns/)) |
| **Technical support/services** | Support for professional energy-system customers, remotely and on site. | Specialist trade customers → installers and their end customers. | Direct service relationship. **Countries and whether each service is separately charged are not stated.** ([ritter-energie.de](https://ritter-energie.de/)) |

For **Ritter XL Solar**, the directory’s declared **EEA markets** are Denmark, Germany, Finland, France, Ireland, Italy, Netherlands, Norway, Austria, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Sweden, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Czechia and Hungary. It also lists numerous non-EEA markets. The directory is undated and should not be treated as a verified current sales ledger. ([greentech-bw.de](https://greentech-bw.de/en/atlas/companies/ritter-xl-solar-gmbh))

## 5. Museum Ritter: do not automatically count it as a Ritter Sport business

Although Ritter Sport’s visitor website promotes **Museum Ritter**, the museum’s own imprint identifies its operator as the **Marli Hoppe-Ritter Foundation for the Promotion of Art**, a charitable foundation—not Alfred Ritter GmbH & Co. KG. Its exhibitions and cultural activities therefore belong in a related-organisation inventory, not automatically in the company’s commercial activities. The neighbouring museum café likewise should not be attributed to the chocolate company without confirming its operator. ([ritter-sport.com](https://www.ritter-sport.com/waldenbuch))

### Bottom line

Ritter Sport’s publicly documented activities extend beyond packaged chocolate to **wafer confectionery, cocoa-fruit beverages, corporate promotional products, custom manufacture, workshops, bistro/event services, non-food merchandise, farming, internal energy generation and a historical digital-collectible project**. **PURmacherei’s non-chocolate snack business has closed.** Related family energy companies operate substantial heating and solar businesses, but their legal scope must be kept separate. Most importantly, **the public sources do not provide a complete country-of-sale list for each activity**, so the “100+ countries” statement should not be applied indiscriminately to beverages, merchandise, workshops or energy products. ([ritter-sport.com](https://www.ritter-sport.com/about-us))

# Barry Callebaut: business activities and routes to market

**Barry Callebaut is principally a business-to-business ingredients and solutions supplier—not a conventional consumer chocolate retailer. Its activities extend well beyond chocolate and cocoa to nuts, biscuits and meringues, caramel, sugar decorations, food colours, coffee/tea and milk-based beverage mixes, cocoa-fruit ingredients, professional training, and agricultural development.** Its annual report groups these activities into **Global Cocoa**, **Global Chocolate**, and **Corporate and other**; “Global Chocolate” includes non-chocolate products such as vending beverages. ([financialfilings.com](https://financialfilings.com/filings/barry-callebaut-ag/annual-report/2025/50597908/))

## Scope and evidence limitations

This inventory covers the **distinct commercial product and service activities disclosed publicly**, plus upstream farming and sourcing activities. It is not a list of every recipe or SKU.

I used the company’s website and **Annual Report 2024/25** first. That is the latest annual report available as of **October 14, 2026**: the company schedules its 2025/26 full-year results for **November 4, 2026**. The official annual-report PDF was too large for the browser to retrieve in full, so I also consulted a searchable reproduction of the same company report. Other sources are used below only to add country or channel information. ([barry-callebaut.com](https://www.barry-callebaut.com/en/about-us/media/news-stories/barry-callebaut-group-full-year-results-fiscal-year-2024-25))

**Important geographical distinction:** factory locations, ingredient origins, website language options, and countries where a customer sells a finished product are not necessarily countries where Barry Callebaut itself sells an ingredient. I distinguish these below. Where the reviewed sources do not identify countries of sale, I say so explicitly.

## 1. Chocolate, cocoa and related ingredients

| Activity / product or service | Who buys directly from Barry Callebaut? | Ultimate user or consumer; how it reaches them | Countries of sale, especially EEA |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Industrial chocolate and couverture:** dark, milk, white, ruby, origin-specific, caramelised and other specialised chocolate formulations; ingredients for confectionery, bakery, ice cream and desserts. | Food manufacturers, including large multinational and regional manufacturers. The company also enters long-term supply/outsourcing arrangements. | Consumers eat customers’ branded or private-label confectionery, baked goods, ice cream and desserts. Barry Callebaut’s sale is **B2B to manufacturers**; downstream supermarket/retail and foodservice sales belong to its customers. | Sales are reported across Western Europe, Central/Eastern Europe, North America, Latin America, and Asia-Pacific/Middle East/Africa. **A complete country-by-product list, including an EEA list, is not stated.** ([barry-callebaut.com](https://www.barry-callebaut.com/en/about-us/media/news-stories/barry-callebaut-group-full-year-results-fiscal-year-2024-25)) |
| **Professional/artisan chocolate and cocoa:** couverture, callets, blocks and other professional formats, marketed through Callebaut, Cacao Barry, Carma, Chocovic and other regional brands. | Distributors/wholesalers and professional users—chocolatiers, pastry chefs, bakers, ice-cream makers, hotels, restaurants and caterers. | Professionals transform the ingredients into products sold in their shops, restaurants, hotels and catering businesses. Home bakers can also obtain products through independent distributors; the company’s website has a hobby-buyer distributor locator. | The current locator identifies **Belgium, Czechia, France, Germany, Italy, Netherlands and Poland** individually, plus **Iberia, Nordics and Balkans** as regional markets. It also identifies numerous non-EEA markets, listed in section 4 below. **This is not proof that every product is sold in every listed market.** ([barry-callebaut.com](https://www.barry-callebaut.com/en/about-us/media/news-stories/barry-callebaut-group-9-month-key-sales-figures-fiscal-year-202526)) |
| **Cocoa processing and cocoa ingredients:** cocoa liquor/mass, cocoa butter and cocoa powder; cocoa ingredients for industrial and professional applications. Cocoa butter also has culinary uses, including the Mycryo frying product. | Food manufacturers and professional users; substantial cocoa output also goes internally to the group’s chocolate business. | Consumers ultimately eat or drink the resulting chocolate, bakery, dessert and beverage products. Sales are industrial B2B and professional ingredient distribution—not necessarily retail cocoa products sold directly by the group. | Global Cocoa is a worldwide business, but **a complete external-sales country list and separate EEA list for each cocoa ingredient are not stated**. Internal transfers are not external customer sales. ([financialfilings.com](https://financialfilings.com/filings/barry-callebaut-ag/annual-report/2025/50597908/)) |
| **Compound/cacao coatings and glazes:** coatings using alternative fat systems, including products for bakery, confectionery and ice cream. Some contain cocoa; this category should not automatically be called cocoa-free. | Food manufacturers and professional foodservice/artisan users. | Consumers eat coated confectionery, bakery products and ice cream; sold B2B as ingredients and then through customers’ retail or foodservice channels. | **Complete countries of sale are not stated.** A company announcement specifically confirms Van Houten Professional compound distribution to foodservice professionals in **Indonesia**. ([barry-callebaut.com](https://www.barry-callebaut.com/en/about-us/media/news-stories/barry-callebaut-group-9-month-key-sales-figures-fiscal-year-202526)) |
| **Chocolate fillings, inclusions and decorations:** fillings, solid/filled pieces, curls, shells and decorative components, including Mona Lisa and Gertrude Hawk Ingredients products. | Food manufacturers, professional artisans and distributors serving them. | Consumers eat the inclusions/decorations in ice cream, snacks, baked goods, confectionery and plated desserts. Sold as ingredients/components, not necessarily as finished consumer confectionery. | **A complete country or EEA sales list is not stated.** The company positions Gertrude Hawk Ingredients within its Americas specialties business and Mona Lisa within its international decoration portfolio. ([barry-callebaut.com](https://www.barry-callebaut.com/en/artisans/gertrude-hawk)) |

## 2. Activities outside conventional chocolate and cocoa

These are separate product activities, even where the ingredients are used together with chocolate.

| Activity / product or service | Who buys directly? | Ultimate consumer and sales route | Countries of sale, especially EEA |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Nut ingredients — La Morella Nuts and American Almond:** nuts, chopped nuts, pure nut pastes, pralinés, nut butters, nut flours, caramelised nuts, crunchy toppings and bake-stable fillings. | Industrial food manufacturers and professional customers in confectionery, pastry, bakery, ice cream and beverages; distributors serving these users. | Consumers eat them in confectionery, baked goods, ice cream, snacks and drinks. Home bakers are also identified as users of American Almond products. Primarily B2B ingredients, subsequently sold through customers’ retail/foodservice channels. | La Morella’s company disclosure identifies **Europe**, with historical expansion to Russia and Asia, but no complete current country list. A **2017** trade report adds **Belgium, France and Spain** as major markets; this is historical evidence, not a current exhaustive list. American Almond’s company disclosure confirms the **United States/North America**; **its EEA sales countries are not stated**. ([barry-callebaut.com](https://www.barry-callebaut.com/en-SG/about-us/media/news-stories/barry-callebaut-acquires-spanish-company-la-morella-nuts-sa)) |
| **Marzipan and almond-based preparations/decorations:** American Almond marzipan and Dings Decor’s standard or tailor-made marzipan products and figures. American Almond also discloses **cookie mixes**. | Professional bakers, pastry chefs, confectioners, manufacturers and their distributors. | Consumers eat marzipan in cakes/confectionery or as edible decorations; cookie mixes are used to make baked products. Sold as professional ingredients or ready-made edible components. | **Complete countries of sale are not stated; no comprehensive EEA list is provided.** Dings Decor’s Netherlands location is not, by itself, evidence of all its sales destinations. ([barry-callebaut.com](https://www.barry-callebaut.com/en-CA/group/media/news-stories/barry-callebaut-acquire-assets-american-almond)) |
| **Biscuit, cookie, cereal and meringue inclusions — especially D’Orsogna Dolciaria:** amaretti, cookies, biscuit crunch/feuilletine, sponge-cake pieces, meringues and other crunchy inclusions. | Mainly manufacturers of ice cream, dairy and bakery products, alongside gourmet/professional customers. | Consumers eat them in ice cream, yoghurt, snacks, cakes and desserts. Sold B2B as components; the manufacturer or artisan sells the finished food. | Company sources identify **Europe/Western Europe**, but **individual countries of sale and a complete EEA list are not stated**. Italian production does not establish an Italy-only market. ([barry-callebaut.com](https://www.barry-callebaut.com/en-CA/about-us/media/news-stories/barry-callebaut-acquire-dorsogna-dolciaria-leading-specialties-and)) |
| **Caramel and toffee ingredients:** caramel fillings, coatings, sauces/centres and sugar-based caramel/toffee inclusions—not just caramel-flavoured chocolate. | Confectionery, bakery, ice-cream and dairy manufacturers; professional pastry/confectionery users. | Consumers eat them within filled, coated or topped foods and desserts. Sold directly as industrial ingredients or through professional ingredient distribution. | **Countries of sale are not stated** on the reviewed caramel range pages; **no complete EEA list is supplied**. ([barry-callebaut.com](https://www.barry-callebaut.com/en-GB/manufacturers/products/caramel-range-fillings-coatings-decorations-inclusions-and-more)) |
| **Sugar-based icing and decoration products:** Carma fondant and sugar-based decorative preparations. | Professional bakers, pastry chefs, cake decorators and distributors. | Consumers eat the icing/decorations on cakes and pastries. Sold in professional ingredient packs—for example, the current Carma white fondant listing specifies a **15 kg pail**. | **Countries of sale are not stated** for the reviewed product; a global product page is not sufficient proof of availability in every EEA country. ([callebaut.com](https://www.callebaut.com/en/products/carma/fondant/COW-62FONDANT-Z37)) |
| **Food colours, decorative printing and transfer sheets — Mona Lisa Studio / IBC:** edible colour preparations, coloured cocoa butter, sugar-based prints, transfer sheets and custom seasonal/personalised decoration solutions. | Artisans, pastry chefs, chocolatiers and industrial food manufacturers, directly or through professional suppliers. | Consumers eat the transferred edible design/colour or decorated food; the carrier sheet itself is a production aid, not food. Products support B2B decoration and customisation. | **A complete country/EEA sales list is not stated.** The group identifies Mona Lisa Studio as the successor to IBC in Belgium; that production location does not establish all destinations. ([barry-callebaut.com](https://www.barry-callebaut.com/fr-CG/trends-insights/easy-personalization-and-seasonality-transfer-sheets)) |
| **Coffee/cappuccino beverage mixes — Caprimo and Satro:** instant cappuccino and flavoured cappuccino/coffee-style drinks. | Vending operators and beverage/foodservice distributors; professional beverage users. Exact direct-buyer arrangements are not disclosed for every SKU. | Consumers drink them from vending machines and in foodservice settings. The ingredient is sold in professional bags/cartons, then prepared and sold by the operator. | Caprimo is explicitly positioned in the **European market**, but **a full country list, including EEA countries, is not stated**. ([barry-callebaut.com](https://www.barry-callebaut.com/en/brands)) |
| **Tea and fruit-drink mixes:** Caprimo lemon tea and wild-fruit drink; Satro mint, lemon and wild-berry instant teas. | Vending/beverage distributors and operators; professional foodservice users. | Consumers drink prepared hot or cold beverages. Sold as mixes for dispensing/preparation, rather than necessarily as bottled consumer drinks. | **Countries of sale are not explicitly stated.** A Netherlands-localised catalogue displays the products, but localisation alone is not conclusive evidence of actual sales. ([barry-callebaut.com](https://www.barry-callebaut.com/nl-NL/vending/products?categories_level_1%5B0%5D=92)) |
| **Milk-based beverage ingredients:** milk powders, granulated skimmed milk and vending “toppings”—here meaning the milk/foam component of a drink, not cake decorations. Includes Satro and Le Royal products. | Vending operators, beverage distributors and professional beverage users. | Consumers drink them in coffee, cocoa and other milk-based drinks. Sold in professional ingredient packs for machines or preparation. | **The company does not provide a complete country list.** Independent online sellers demonstrate availability in **Germany** and **Poland**, both EEA countries. These establish reseller availability, not the identities of Barry Callebaut’s direct buyers. ([barry-callebaut.com](https://www.barry-callebaut.com/en-EE/vending/products?categories_level_1%5B0%5D=87&categories_level_2%5B0%5D=89)) |
| **Chocolate/cocoa drink mixes — Van Houten and other beverage brands:** drinking chocolate and cocoa-based vending/foodservice preparations. | Retail-channel customers, HoReCa users, vending operators and distributors; arrangements vary by market. | Consumers drink them at home, in cafés/hotels/restaurants or from vending machines. Unlike most industrial ingredients, the brand description expressly includes **retail**. | Van Houten says **more than 40 countries**, but **does not name the full list or identify all EEA countries**. ([barry-callebaut.com](https://www.barry-callebaut.com/en/brands)) |
| **Non-bean cocoa-fruit ingredients — Cacaofruit, previously Cabosse Naturals:** pulp, juice and juice concentrate for beverages, sorbets and other foods. Its powder offering also includes a pulp/cocoa-powder blend, so not every product is outside cocoa. | Food and beverage manufacturers and professional ingredient/application partners. | Consumers eat or drink customers’ beverages, sorbets, ice cream and other foods. Barry Callebaut sells ingredients, rather than necessarily selling the finished drink directly to consumers. | **A complete ingredient-sales country list is not stated.** A disclosed partner application—Rogelfrut cocoa-fruit gelato mix—was made available to artisans/gelaterias in **Italy from May 2021**. That confirms downstream Italian availability, not an exhaustive Barry Callebaut sales list. ([barry-callebaut.com](https://www.barry-callebaut.com/fr-CA/trends-insights/consumers-are-seeking-ways-nurture-their-nature)) |
| **Cocoa-free chocolate alternatives — ChoViva:** sunflower-seed-based chocolate-like ingredients supplied through the commercial partnership with Planet A Foods. | Food manufacturers seeking cocoa-free ingredient/coating solutions. | Consumers eat customers’ confectionery, bakery and other finished products. Barry Callebaut acts through a B2B commercial partnership; it does **not own Planet A Foods merely because of this partnership**. | The company announcement identifies **Europe** and intended global expansion, **not a complete country list**. Additional reporting confirms a **US introduction in May 2026**. Planet A Foods confirms downstream products in **Germany and France**—EEA—and the UK, but those launches predate the partnership and cannot all be attributed to Barry Callebaut sales. ([barry-callebaut.com](https://www.barry-callebaut.com/system/files/2025-11/Press%20Release%20-%20Barry%20Callebaut%20and%20Planet%20A%20Foods%20Announcement%20-%20EN.pdf)) |

## 3. Services and upstream business activities

### A. Product development, co-creation and application support

- **Service:** customised recipes/formulations, technical application help, co-creation, processing support and marketing/inspiration resources.
- **Direct customer:** food manufacturers and professional artisans/foodservice businesses.
- **Ultimate beneficiary:** the customer’s business; consumers benefit indirectly through resulting foods.
- **How sold:** customer relationships and tailored programmes. The reviewed sources **do not consistently separate paid consultancy from support bundled into ingredient sales**.
- **Countries:** offered through the international customer/academy network; **a separate service-sales country list is not stated**. ([cloudflare.barry-callebaut.com](https://cloudflare.barry-callebaut.com/sites/default/files/2019-01/barry-callebaut-gri-report-2013-14.pdf))

### B. Professional education — Chocolate Academy

- **Service:** paid in-person masterclasses, practical courses, bespoke/team programmes, and free online tutorials.
- **Direct buyer/user:** chefs, artisans and businesses booking training; online learners use the free resources directly.
- **Ultimate consumer:** the learner consumes the service; food consumers benefit indirectly.
- **How sold:** direct course registration through the academy network, with online learning delivered through its website.
- **Countries:** the current locations page explicitly identifies EEA centres in **Belgium, France, Italy, Poland, Spain and the Netherlands**. It also identifies centres outside the EEA, including the US, Canada, Brazil, Switzerland, Russia and other markets. **It does not state a complete country list for online learners or paid-service purchasers.** ([chocolate-academy.com](https://www.chocolate-academy.com/en/learning))

### C. Raw-material sourcing and cocoa procurement

- **Activity:** purchasing cocoa and other chocolate ingredients, including sugar, dairy and nuts; cocoa processing and supply to both external customers and the group’s own production.
- **Buyer/output user:** principally Barry Callebaut’s own manufacturing operations, plus external cocoa-ingredient customers.
- **Ultimate consumer:** consumers of resulting food/beverage products.
- **Route:** upstream procurement, internal transfers and external B2B ingredient sales.
- **Countries:** **procurement origins are not countries of sale**. The annual report does not provide a separate exhaustive country list for external raw-material trading. It should not be assumed that sourcing sugar or dairy means operating a broad standalone sugar/dairy retail business. ([financialfilings.com](https://financialfilings.com/filings/barry-callebaut-ag/annual-report/2025/50597908/))

### D. Farming, nurseries and agricultural development

- **Activity:** the Future Farming Initiative, cocoa farming trials/partnerships, seedling production, agricultural automation and farming services supporting productivity and sustainability.
- **Direct buyer:** **not established as a general external retail/service customer base** in the reviewed disclosures; these activities principally develop and secure the supply chain.
- **Ultimate user:** farmers, farming partners and the group’s cocoa supply chain; consumers benefit indirectly.
- **Route:** farm partnerships, nurseries, technical programmes and supply-chain collaboration—not supermarkets or consumer shops.
- **Countries:** disclosed activity includes **Bahia, Brazil**, and an **own farm in Ecuador**. These are operating locations; **countries of external sales, including EEA sales, are not stated**. The 2024/25 impact report reports 1.5 million seedlings produced, but does not establish that all were sold externally. ([barry-callebaut.com](https://www.barry-callebaut.com/system/files/2025-11/Annual%20Social%20and%20Environmental%20Impact%20Report%202024_25_3.pdf))

## 4. What can actually be established about EEA sales?

The strongest current company evidence for named markets is its **professional-product distributor locator**:

- **Individually named EEA markets:** Belgium, Czechia, France, Germany, Italy, Netherlands and Poland.
- **Regional entries requiring caution:** Iberia, Nordics and Balkans. These must not be expanded into a definitive country-by-country list without additional distributor evidence.
- **Other individually named markets:** Switzerland, Russia, Türkiye, Ukraine, Brazil, Canada, United States, China, India, Japan and South Korea; other regions include British Isles, Australia/New Zealand, Latin America, Mexico/Caribbean, Southeast Asia, Africa and Middle East. ([callebaut.com](https://www.callebaut.com/en/products/where-to-buy/map?popup=true&type=hobby))

**This locator supports the existence of a distribution route—not the claim that every Barry Callebaut activity or SKU is sold in all those markets.** For nuts, caramel, decorations, tea/coffee mixes, cocoa-fruit ingredients and cocoa-free alternatives, the public sources generally do **not** disclose a complete current EEA sales matrix.

## 5. Consumer sales and businesses not to confuse with the group

- **No general own-shop or direct-to-consumer online retail chain was established in the reviewed current disclosures.** A product available from an independent online seller is not a direct Barry Callebaut consumer sale; its own “where to buy” page points buyers to distributors. ([callebaut.com](https://www.callebaut.com/en/products/where-to-buy/map?popup=true&type=hobby))
- Barry Callebaut sold its **European consumer-products business, Stollwerck**, in **September 2011**. Historical consumer brands from that business should not be counted automatically as current activities. ([barry-callebaut.com](https://www.barry-callebaut.com/sites/default/files/2019-01/annual_report_201011_e_0.pdf))
- The relevant acquired business is **Gertrude Hawk Ingredients**; evidence about that ingredients business should not be used to attribute all Gertrude Hawk consumer shops to Barry Callebaut. ([barry-callebaut.com](https://www.barry-callebaut.com/en-US/about-us/media/news-stories/full-year-results-fiscal-year-201718-barry-callebaut-group))
- I found **no sufficient company-specific evidence** to classify cosmetics, pharmaceuticals, household products, or general-purpose retail sale of sugar/oils as separate current Barry Callebaut businesses. Generic uses of cocoa butter or palm oil are not evidence that the company sells into those sectors.

**Bottom line:** the disclosed portfolio is considerably broader than chocolate, but public reporting does not support an exhaustive activity-by-country sales list. The tables above identify the disclosed activities and channels while keeping confirmed sales markets, regional descriptions, historical evidence and unstated geography separate.

# Bahlsen — business activities and routes to market

**Bahlsen is primarily a packaged sweet-baked-goods business, not a supplier of cocoa or chocolate ingredients. Its activities also include private-label products, organic fruit-and-nut/protein bars, direct retailing of other manufacturers’ foods, and branded merchandise.** Food-innovation services appear in older group reporting but should not automatically be treated as a current Bahlsen activity. ([handelsregister.ai](https://handelsregister.ai/zh/organizations/hannover/herstellung-von-dauerbackwaren/bisquiva-gmbh-co-kg-6e45ae0942e5dcace377d18dfc8c198e))

## Scope and evidence limitations

I interpret “Bahlsen” as **Bahlsen GmbH & Co. KG and its controlled businesses**, rather than just products carrying the Bahlsen brand. The company’s current brand page lists **Bahlsen, LEIBNIZ, PiCK UP!, Brandt, Krakuski, HIT and RAWBITE**; Bisquiva separately identifies itself as a wholly owned Bahlsen subsidiary. ([bahlsen.com](https://www.bahlsen.com/de/thebahlsenfamily/marken/))

I prioritized company and subsidiary websites, then company financial reporting. A filing index identifies **2024 consolidated accounts, published March 19, 2026**, but I could not access their full contents. I examined accessible **2021 consolidated accounts and management reporting**, reproduced by a registry-data service. Accordingly, this is **all business activity identifiable from the accessible evidence—not a guarantee that every current subsidiary or incidental revenue stream has been disclosed**. Historical activities are marked separately. ([unternehmen24.info](https://www.unternehmen24.info/Handelsregister/Deutschland/Bilanz/Firma/1714533/Jahresabschluss%202024))

## 1. Manufacture and sale of branded biscuits, wafers and sweet pastries

**Product.** Packaged biscuits, cookies, sandwich biscuits, wafers, puff pastries and biscuit assortments, both with and without chocolate/cocoa. Non-chocolate examples include LEIBNIZ butter biscuits and Bahlsen ABC Russisch Brot, fruit-filled Deloba, sugar-coated Blätterbrezeln, nut-and-vanilla Kipferl and Butterblätter. The group markets these categories through its biscuit brands, including Brandt, Krakuski and HIT—not just the Bahlsen name. ([bahlsen.com](https://www.bahlsen.com/de/thebahlsenfamily/marken/))

**Direct buyers.** Retail trade customers and distributors are the identifiable commercial customer categories. The group’s management report describes sales through its parent and national sales subsidiaries, with distributors serving additional export markets. **The sources do not identify the contractual first buyer for every retailer or country**; a supermarket stocking a product does not necessarily buy directly from Bahlsen. Consumers also buy directly in Bahlsen outlets, discussed below. ([handelsregister.ai](https://handelsregister.ai/zh/organizations/hannover/herstellung-von-dauerbackwaren/bisquiva-gmbh-co-kg-6e45ae0942e5dcace377d18dfc8c198e))

**Ultimate consumers and sales channels.** Individuals and households eat the products. They reach consumers through food retail, third-party online retail and Bahlsen outlets. For example, Bahlsen’s US website directs consumers to physical stores, the Loacker US shop, Amazon and Walmart; these links do **not** establish that all those purchases are direct sales by Bahlsen. ([bahlsen.com](https://www.bahlsen.com/en-us/?page_id=34))

**Countries.** Bahlsen states that its products are marketed in **more than 80 countries**, but **does not publish a complete country-of-sale list or a country-by-product matrix in the reviewed pages**. Country evidence is consolidated in the geographic section below. Its international website explicitly warns that products may be unavailable in a particular country or sold under a different brand. ([bahlsen.com](https://www.bahlsen.com/de/thebahlsenfamily/marken/))

## 2. Manufacture and sale of biscuit-based snack bars

**Product.** PiCK UP! biscuit-and-chocolate snack bars, including mini formats and filled variants. This is a finished consumer-snack business, distinct from supplying chocolate to food manufacturers or artisans. ([bahlsen.com](https://www.bahlsen.com/en-us/?page_id=34))

**Direct buyers, ultimate consumers and channels.** The branded-products distribution structure above applies: trade customers/distributors and, through outlets, consumers directly. Consumers eat the bars as snacks. They are also supplied through a documented UK foodservice distributor. ([handelsregister.ai](https://handelsregister.ai/zh/organizations/hannover/herstellung-von-dauerbackwaren/bisquiva-gmbh-co-kg-6e45ae0942e5dcace377d18dfc8c198e))

**Countries.** Germany is evidenced through Bahlsen’s outlet assortment, the US through its country website, and the UK through its foodservice distributor. **A complete PiCK UP!-specific country-of-sale list is not stated.** ([celle-tourismus.de](https://www.celle-tourismus.de/sehenswuerdigkeiten/bahlsen-outlet-celle))

## 3. Manufacture and sale of packaged cakes

**Product.** Ready-to-eat packaged cakes, notably **Comtess**: lemon, poppy-seed/lemon, marble, chocolate, hazelnut, marzipan and other varieties. This includes substantial activity outside chocolate/cocoa—for example, lemon cakes with light icing. ([bahlsen.com](https://www.bahlsen.com/de/produkte/))

**Direct buyers and ultimate consumers.** Trade customers/distributors under the group’s branded baked-goods model; consumers ultimately eat the cakes. **Cake-specific direct-customer contracts are not disclosed.** ([handelsregister.ai](https://handelsregister.ai/zh/organizations/hannover/herstellung-von-dauerbackwaren/bisquiva-gmbh-co-kg-6e45ae0942e5dcace377d18dfc8c198e))

**Sales channels and countries.** Packaged retail sales are evidenced by the German product range. **Germany is confirmed; a complete cake-specific country list and detailed channel split are not stated.** The group-wide “80-plus countries” claim should not be applied to every cake variety. ([bahlsen.com](https://www.bahlsen.com/de/produkte/))

## 4. Manufacture and sale of seasonal baked goods

**Product.** Christmas/winter biscuits, gingerbread, cinnamon stars, speculoos, filled gingerbread, mini stollen, seasonal cakes and confectionery-style baked pieces. Non-chocolate products include white-iced cinnamon stars, almond/spiced/butter speculoos, and poppy-seed or marzipan mini stollen. The German site describes its winter assortment as available September–December. ([bahlsen.com](https://www.bahlsen.com/de/produkte/))

**Direct buyers, ultimate consumers and channels.** Trade buyers/distributors and outlet consumers; individuals and households ultimately consume the products. Seasonal retail and outlet sales are evidenced. ([handelsregister.ai](https://handelsregister.ai/zh/organizations/hannover/herstellung-von-dauerbackwaren/bisquiva-gmbh-co-kg-6e45ae0942e5dcace377d18dfc8c198e))

**Countries.** The German range confirms Germany. **The complete countries of sale for seasonal goods are not stated**, and availability varies by market. ([bahlsen.com](https://www.bahlsen.com/de/produkte/))

## 5. Private-label product supply and development — Bisquiva

**Product/service.** Customized private-label sweet products: **biscuits and coffee pastries, wafers, Jaffa cakes, mini biscuits and peppermint tablets**. Bisquiva also offers expertise to implement customers’ product ideas and develop tailored solutions. Peppermint tablets are an additional confectionery activity beyond baked biscuits; the reviewed category page does not establish that every tablet formulation is cocoa-free. ([bisquiva.com](https://www.bisquiva.com/sortiment.html))

**Direct buyers.** Bisquiva explicitly identifies **international retail chains** as customers. This is a B2B private-label supply activity. **Direct supply to food manufacturers or artisans is not established by the reviewed sources.** ([bisquiva.com](https://www.bisquiva.com/unternehmen.html?lang=de))

**Ultimate consumers and channels.** Consumers buy and eat the resulting private-label products through the customer retailers. Bisquiva supplies the retail businesses rather than operating the consumer-facing brand sale. ([bisquiva.com](https://www.bisquiva.com/unternehmen.html?lang=de))

**Countries.** Bisquiva says it serves customers **worldwide, with a European-market focus**. **Individual countries of sale, including an EEA breakdown, are not stated.** ([bisquiva.com](https://www.bisquiva.com/unternehmen.html?lang=de))

## 6. Organic fruit-and-nut bars and protein bars — RAWBITE

**Product.** Organic, vegan, gluten-free fruit-and-nut snack bars, including non-cocoa flavors and protein variants; multipacks, trial boxes and office boxes are also offered. The current site says the bars are made in Germany—older reporting placed production in Denmark. ([rawbite.de](https://rawbite.de/))

**Direct buyers.** Consumers buy directly from RAWBITE’s webshop. Retail distribution is also confirmed, but **the first-buyer relationship—retailer versus intermediary—is not specified for each chain**. The website has a B2B entry point, although its accessible page did not provide a detailed customer-category list. ([rawbite.de](https://www.rawbite.de/policies/terms-of-service))

**Ultimate consumers and channels.** Consumers eat the bars, including as portable snacks or around sport. Channels include RAWBITE’s own online store, supermarkets, drugstores and organic/specialist stores. The company names German retailers including Alnatura, Denns, Rossmann, Müller, Globus, Kaufland, EDEKA and REWE. Its terms also provide for recurring subscription deliveries. ([rawbite.de](https://rawbite.de/))

**Countries.** RAWBITE states sales in **more than 30 countries**, but **does not enumerate the complete list**. Its German webshop terms explicitly restrict B2C offers and deliveries to **Germany and Austria**. Denmark and Sweden appear in its country selector, but that alone is not proof of delivery coverage for every product. ([rawbite.de](https://rawbite.de/))

## 7. Foodservice distribution of finished biscuits and bars

**Product.** Finished branded snacks supplied for out-of-home consumption. Portion Solutions lists Choco Leibniz, PiCK UP! and Messino and states that it exclusively distributes Bahlsen biscuits in the **UK foodservice channel**. ([portionsolutions.co.uk](https://www.portionsolutions.co.uk/Bahlsen))

**Direct buyers.** The documented route is through a **foodservice distributor**, which supplies operators downstream. **Direct Bahlsen sales to individual hotels, cafés or caterers are not established.** ([portionsolutions.co.uk](https://www.portionsolutions.co.uk/Bahlsen))

**Ultimate consumers and channel.** Foodservice patrons eat the snacks; sales pass through the distributor into the foodservice channel. ([portionsolutions.co.uk](https://www.portionsolutions.co.uk/Bahlsen))

**Countries.** **UK confirmed—not an EEA country.** A US foodservice wholesaler’s inventory also lists Bahlsen products, but does not establish direct procurement from Bahlsen. **An EEA-wide foodservice country list is not stated.** ([portionsolutions.co.uk](https://www.portionsolutions.co.uk/Bahlsen))

## 8. Own-store retailing, including other manufacturers’ foods

**Product/service.** Bahlsen operates discount outlets selling its own brands and selected third-party brands. Assortments include first- and second-quality goods and products normally sold abroad. Importantly, the retail activity extends to **salty snacks/chips, fruit gums, chocolate, pralines, marzipan, cereal bars and jam**, with brands such as Lorenz, Lindt, Corny, Suntjens and Schwartau. These are **resale activities, not evidence that Bahlsen manufactures those third-party products**. ([bahlsen.com](https://www.bahlsen.com/de/thebahlsenfamily/unternehmen/standorte/))

**Direct buyers and ultimate consumers.** Shoppers purchase directly from the outlet operator; they or gift recipients consume the goods. The Hannover market-hall listing identifies Bahlsen GmbH & Co. KG as operator. ([markthalle-in-hannover.de](https://markthalle-in-hannover.de/bahlsen-outlet/))

**Channel and countries.** Physical own shops in **Germany**. The outlet website currently lists **29 locations**, whereas the corporate location page says 28. **No outlet countries outside Germany are identified in the reviewed sources.** ([bahlsen-outlet.de](https://www.bahlsen-outlet.de/filialfinder))

## 9. Non-food merchandise — RAWBITE

**Product.** RAWBITE-branded organic-quality hoodies and fabric tote bags. ([rawbite.de](https://www.rawbite.de/collections/merchandise))

**Direct buyers and ultimate users.** Consumers buy directly online; purchasers or gift recipients wear/use the items. ([rawbite.de](https://rawbite.de/products/rawbite-hoodie-in-bio-qualitat))

**Channel and countries.** RAWBITE’s own webshop. Its B2C terms identify **Germany and Austria** as the delivery countries. **A separate worldwide merchandise distribution list is not stated.** ([rawbite.de](https://www.rawbite.de/collections/merchandise))

## Geographic findings, especially the EEA

| Evidence level | Countries/territories | What can safely be concluded |
|---|---|---|
| Dedicated Bahlsen consumer-market websites | **EEA:** Germany, Austria, Italy, Poland. **Outside EEA:** UK, US | Named consumer markets; not proof that every product category is sold in each. ([bahlsen.com](https://www.bahlsen.com/welcome/)) |
| Additional commercial-market organization | **EEA:** Belgium, Luxembourg, Ireland | Belgium and Luxembourg have listed business units; Ireland is explicitly part of “UK & Ireland.” These do not supply category-level sales lists. ([bahlsen.com](https://www.bahlsen.com/de/thebahlsenfamily/unternehmen/standorte/)) |
| RAWBITE direct online delivery | **EEA:** Germany, Austria | Explicitly stated delivery coverage under the reviewed webshop terms. ([rawbite.de](https://www.rawbite.de/policies/terms-of-service)) |
| Own outlets | **EEA:** Germany | Explicit physical retail coverage. ([bahlsen-outlet.de](https://www.bahlsen-outlet.de/filialfinder)) |
| Global claims | Bahlsen: **80-plus countries**; RAWBITE: **30-plus**; Bisquiva: worldwide, Europe-focused | **Complete country lists and EEA-by-activity breakdowns are not stated.** ([bahlsen.com](https://www.bahlsen.com/de/thebahlsenfamily/marken/)) |

The offices in **China, Singapore and the UAE** indicate commercial presence, but an office address alone is not sufficient to establish the countries of sale for each activity. ([bahlsen.com](https://www.bahlsen.com/de/thebahlsenfamily/unternehmen/standorte/))

## Historical or unresolved activities—not confirmed as current

- **Food-innovation support/KitchenTown:** The 2021 management report describes advice and support for food production and market launch through KitchenTown. Direct customers were food startups/businesses; these were B2B services rather than consumer foods, based in Berlin. However, the successor’s own website says KitchenTown Berlin’s operations ended in **2025**, the space was transferred to vly, and an **independent** FutureFoodCo began in **January 2026**. I therefore do **not** count FutureFoodCo as a current Bahlsen business. The historical service countries are not fully stated. ([handelsregister.ai](https://handelsregister.ai/zh/organizations/hannover/herstellung-von-dauerbackwaren/bisquiva-gmbh-co-kg-6e45ae0942e5dcace377d18dfc8c198e))
- **Insurance intermediation:** Older accounts name a participation called Bahlsen Versicherungs-Vermittlung GmbH. They do not establish its current external services, buyers or sale countries; the entity’s name alone is insufficient to describe an active customer-facing business. ([uploads1.craft.co](https://uploads1.craft.co/uploads/craft/source/document/23791/835f1d6561c6c6a0.pdf))
- **Salty-snack manufacturing:** Lorenz is a separate independent business. Bahlsen’s resale of Lorenz goods through outlets must not be confused with ownership of Lorenz’s manufacturing activities. ([edeka-convenience.de](https://edeka-convenience.de/industrie-und-markenpartner/lorenz-bahlsen/))

**Remaining gap:** Public sources establish the principal activities above, but not a complete current legal-entity/activity inventory or every destination country. The full 2024 consolidated report and a company-confirmed country-by-product/channel schedule would be needed to close those gaps.
